standard_prerequisites: Context span 2536-2541 (section-nonfree): R = Q[x] and M = sum over n of (1/(x-n)) R as a submodule of the fraction field; M is not finitely generated, but for every prime p of R we have M_p = R_p as an R_p-module (the author's stalk computation stated in the section)

Context span 2574-2597: A = Sym*_R(M) (an example of a non-Noetherian domain with Noetherian local rings, author's footnote) and I = MA = the direct sum of the Sym^d_R(M) for d >= 1; M not finitely generated implies I is not finitely generated as an ideal, and an invertible module is finitely generated, so I is not invertible; for every prime p of R, M_p = R_p gives A_p = Sym*_{R_p}(R_p) = R_p[T] as a graded R_p-algebra, so I_p is generated by the nonzerodivisor T; hence for every prime q of A the ideal I_q is generated by a single element
core_obligations: A is a domain (context: Sym of a torsion-free module over the domain R) and I = MA is a nonzero ideal
I is not invertible because it is not finitely generated (context chain: M not finitely generated, invertible implies finitely generated)
For every prime q of A the localization I_q is principal (context: at p = q intersect R the algebra is R_p[T] and I_p = (T))
proof_roadmap: Take A = Sym*_R(M) and I = MA from the context
Non-invertibility from the non-finite-generation chain in the context
Principal-at-every-prime from the context stalk identification
